messages:
raj (FinServApp): Hey support — our integration started returning 400s from the /call-tool endpoint when we pass invoice metadata. Error: \"Invalid JSON input: Unexpected token at position 43\". Happened after a customer pasted an internal note into the description field.

alice.support: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact payload you sent (scrub PII) and the curl / SDK call you used?

raj (FinServApp): Sure — here's the payload we send (we replaced numbers with X):

```json
{
  "tool": "submit_invoice",
  "args": {
    "invoice_id": "INV-XXXX",
    "amount": 1234.56,
    "description": "Payment for subscription\u000b #12345 - thanks!"
  }
}
```

We send this from Node: `fetch(url, {method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'}, body: JSON.stringify(payload) })`.

ben.eng: Interesting — that looks like a vertical tab (\u000b) inside the string. Per RFC, certain control chars must be escaped in JSON. But if you already have the literal vertical tab character in a JS string and then JSON.stringify it, it should escape to \u000b. Is the client perhaps double-encoding or using a raw string?

raj (FinServApp): The customer pasted from an editor that may have inserted an actual control char. I inspected logs and the body we receive on our side has the literal VT (not the escape sequence). Our outgoing request to Redwood has the literal too — maybe our HTTP library isn't escaping?

carol-sre: On the server side I see the request body hit the edge and the parser threw at byte 43. The raw bytes contain 0x0B at that position. Many JSON parsers will reject unescaped control characters.

alice.support: Can you reproduce by sending a request with an actual VT byte? Small curl example that reproduces locally: 

```bash
echo -e '{"tool":"submit_invoice","args":{"invoice_id":"INV-XXXX","amount":1234.56,"description":"Payment for subscription'$'\x0B'' #12345 - thanks!"}}' | curl -s -XPOST https://api.redwood.example/v1/call-tool -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @-
```

That should show the same 400 with the parser error.

ben.eng: Confirmed locally — replicates. Root cause: unescaped control char in JSON string. Some clients (older SDKs or custom HTTP libs) will send raw bytes without escaping if they build payloads as raw strings.

raj (FinServApp): OK, any workaround for our customer now? They need to be unblocked.

ben.eng: Quick workaround: sanitize user input before JSON.stringify, remove or replace control characters. Example in JS: 

```js
function sanitize(s) { return s.replace(/\p{Cc}/gu, ' '); }
payload.args.description = sanitize(payload.args.description);
body = JSON.stringify(payload);
```

That removes all control chars (category Cc). Alternatively explicitly escape known chars: `replace(/\x0B/g, '\\u000b')`.

alice.support: I've sent the customer the sanitize snippet and asked them to patch their integration. Also suggested they upgrade to our latest SDK (we recently fixed a path that could send raw bytes for pasted text).

sam_pm: For follow-up — let's add a KB article about control characters in tool args and a small validation note in the API docs. Also consider returning a clearer error: \"control character in string at offset X; please escape or remove\" instead of generic parse error.

ben.eng: Agree. I'll open an ENG ticket to: 1) improve error message at the parser layer, 2) add server-side lenient sanitizer behind a feature flag for a week while we onboard customers.

carol-sre: FYI we saw no sign of malicious payloads — looks purely accidental paste. No rate impact.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: eng/escape-json-fix -> canary at 2026-03-18T02:00Z (ticket ENG-4021).

raj (FinServApp): Thanks everyone — customer patched and confirmed calls are now accepted. Marking resolved from our side, will follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

alice.support: Great — closing this escalation. Posting KB link once live. :white_check_mark:
